verdicts.title: Parity Decision Tree Complexity is Greater Than Granularity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We prove a new lower bound on the parity decision tree complexity $\mathsf{D}_{\oplus}(f)$ of a Boolean function $f$. Namely, granularity of the Boolean function $f$ is the smallest $k$ such that all Fourier coefficients of $f$ are integer multiples of $1/2^k$. We show that $\mathsf{D}_{\oplus}(f)\geq k+1$.

verdicts.title: The greedy flip tree of a subword complex
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We describe a canonical spanning tree of the ridge graph of a subword complex on a finite Coxeter group. It is based on properties of greedy facets in subword complexes, defined and studied in this paper. Searching this tree yields an enumeration scheme for the facets of the subword complex. This algorithm extends the greedy flip algorithm for pointed pseudotriangulations of points or convex bodies in the plane.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns 'subword complexes on a finite Coxeter group' and greedy flip enumeration of their facets — a combinatorial-topology object unrelated to Morse–Hedlund factor complexity of binary rows or decision-tree depth. The shared term 'subword' is incidental vocabulary, not interaction with the SC(f) ≤ n·2^{D(f)} claim.
